issue_context.title: Problems with comments in apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go and watch_cache.go
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
I tried reading those files and noticed some issues in the comments.

- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75879 removed the field `Type` from the struct `Config` but did not update the comments that refer to the now-absent field.
- The comment on the `incomingHWM` field of `Config` does not explain what quantity is being high-water-marked.  The word "incoming" looks suggestive but it is not obvious to me what exactly is meant.
- The `Config` struct has a comment that reads like it is about the `watchers` field but it actually precedes the `watcherIdx` field.
- That comment describes a single mapping, but the type of the `watchers` field is a struct that holds two mappings.
- In `watch_cache.go`, some funcs follow the convention that a name ending in "Locked" means the mutex must be held by the caller, but not all.
- In `watch_cache.go` the concurrency prohibition documented for `processEvent` is _not_ documented for the callers of that func.
- As far as I can see, `processEvent` _is_ thread safe.  Perhaps there is a concurrency issue at a higher level?
- In `processEvent` there is a comment "TODO: We should consider moving this lock below after the watchCacheEvent is created" --- and this comment appears after the creation of the watchCacheEvent.
- `watch_cache.go` has comments with unquoted angle brackets, such as `// List returns list of pointers to <storeElement> objects`.  In some cases, such as the one just mentioned, the angle brackets themselves appear to be intended to function as quotes (but don't).

review_comments:
This comment doesn't make any sense to me.

ResourcePrefix is a prefix that is attached to each key of items stored in etcd (underlying DB).
The concept of `Type` was replaced by a function that creates the empty objects, so I changed the lines. Any suggestions to what I should change it to?

We might want to document this further as indicated in the issue:

We `HighWaterMark` the length of the incoming `watchEvent`s channel. Our intent is mainly to keep track of the highest value of this length so that in case we need to debug cases where the channel is getting backed up and events from it are not being popped and removed, we have logs for occurrences of when the highest channel lengths were achieved.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L799

Can we add this line to the documentation:
`The word "incoming" refers to the incoming 'watchEvent's channel length. We HighWaterMark it keep track of the highest value of this length so that in case we need to debug cases where the channel is getting backed up and events from it are not being popped and removed, we have logs for occurrences of when the highest channel lengths were achieved.`
I feel since the issue needed a complete context of incomingHWM , maybe condensing it further will not be beneficial.
I don't understand it. Let's remove and say above that trigger just may be empty.

The earlier comment didn't mention of 2 mapping of the `watchers` field, namely `watcherIdx` and the trigger function, so I updated this. Should I just remove the entire thing to "Trigger just may be empty" ?
